nodes.question: Which microalgal species was noted for its effectiveness in removing DEET from wastewater?
nodes.answer: Chlorella vulgaris was identified as an effective species for removing 73% of 2 mg/L DEET from wastewater.
nodes.paragraph: Microalgal technologies play a huge role in achieving the Sustainable Develop - ment Goals (SDG) of the United Nations (UN), and it directly takes part in SDG-6, Clean Water and Sani - tation , which aims to enhance the availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation on a worldwide scale [20]. This includes reducing pollu - tion, thoroughly treating wastewater, and improving water recycling. According to SDG 6.3, By 2030, it is decided to increase the water quality by reducing pollu - tion (wastewater treatment), eliminating dumping and minimizing the release of toxic substances (emerging contaminants) and reducing by half the percentage of wastewater that is not treated, and significantly boost - ing reuse and recycling globally, [21]. Microalgae have been tested for their phycoremedia - tion potential in removing emerging contaminants like DEET. For the selection of algal species in the phycore - mediation study, the species should possess reason - able tolerance limits and biodegradation potential with fewer bioaccumulation properties. Chlorella vulgaris was identified as one of the candidates that showed promis - ing results for removing 73% of 2 mg/L DEET from the wastewater [22].
